constrains.current_provenance: frozen mechanistic assumption (Krishnan 2003 Table 1 gives modulus/permeability, not thickness)
constrains.how_it_constrains: A sub-voxel cartilage segmentation of a real knee bounds the depth range over which a 0.20 mm superficial zone and a 1.80 mm bulk zone can be placed; with 0.364583 mm in-plane and 0.7 mm slice spacing the sample can resolve a surface band only approximately, so it bounds layer thickness from one side and shows the resolution limit for depth-resolved properties.
constrains.test_it_could_fail: If the measured cartilage thickness distribution were 0.6-0.8 mm, the model's 2.0 mm total tissue thickness would be falsified as a femoral cartilage column.

constrains.current_provenance: frozen mechanistic assumption; no measured value claimed
constrains.how_it_constrains: The tidemark is not labelled in this dataset (cartilage masks stop at the cartilage-bone interface), so the 0.10 mm barrier layer can be bounded only as 'at most the interface resolution', i.e. one to three voxels; a dedicated tidemark dataset is the missing piece.
constrains.test_it_could_fail: Histological tidemark depths of 0.2-0.5 mm would falsify the 0.10 mm frozen barrier thickness.

constrains.current_value_in_model: 0.05 of the 0.73 MPa reference modulus = 36,500 Pa
constrains.current_provenance: modeling choice within a small-strain regime
constrains.how_it_constrains: Supplies the measured image grid (160 x 384 x 384, 0.7 x 0.364583 x 0.364583 mm) on which a later depth-resolved property assignment would be posed, so the stress normalization can be tied to a real femoral condyle rather than a generic 1-D slab.
constrains.test_it_could_fail: If the knee geometry in the segmentation shows contact patches of the order of 1 cm^2 and a film-limited film conductance, the assumed single-column stress step is not representable.

constrains.model_quantity: normalization_strain (=0.05) and REFERENCE_STRESS_PA (=36,500 Pa), the prescribed total-stress step
constrains.how_it_constrains: Gives a measured, public, time-resolved knee loading waveform (adduction moment components, with/without brace) against which the model's single frozen stress step can be compared in magnitude and duty cycle. It bounds the load side, not the tissue side.
constrains.test_it_could_fail: If the measured tibiofemoral load converted to contact stress sits an order of magnitude above or below 36,500 Pa over the stance phase, the frozen normalization is not a representative small-strain operating point.

constrains.model_quantity: drainage_half_time_s (0.528 s in the delivered run)
constrains.how_it_constrains: Gives the contact-duration scale (stance phase in seconds) against which a 0.53 s drainage half-time can be judged: if a real contact dwell is far shorter, the drainage regime the model is probing is not exercised in gait.
constrains.test_it_could_fail: A stance contact dwell of ~0.05 s would make the model's 1 s/10 s/60 s observation times physiologically unreachable for a single step, and the layer conclusion would then be about a regime that gait never visits.

nifti1.axis_orientation: derived from the sform matrix: column 0 has a positive x component, column 2 is pure +z, so the NIfTI x/y axes are left-right and anterior-posterior consistent with a RAS-style frame; the file itself carries no orientation string and the third column has no y component, so this is an inference from the affine, not a declared field
nifti1.descrip_field: mask with corrected affine matrix and two TCs
nifti1.label_to_anatomy_mapping: UNKNOWN - the file header carries no ROI names and the Zenodo record describes only '5-ROI segmentation mask for cartilages and bones' and a '20-ROI atlas for articular cartilages'. Labels are therefore not attributed to cartilage, bone or specific compartments in this audit.

preregistered_plausibility_check.check: if the sample carries a cartilage segmentation, implied femoral/tibial cartilage thickness must fall in 1.0-6.0 mm
preregistered_plausibility_check.why: ROI identity is UNKNOWN, so no label can be declared cartilage. The bounding boxes of every label span the full 140 x 140 mm field of view in two axes, so a bounding box is not a thickness. The derived label volumes (12.7-135.7 cm3) are too large to be a single cartilage compartment and consistent with multi-structure or multi-compartment labels, which is exactly why the check was not forced through.
